utterance: Hi Chloe, I'm the doctor today. I'll check what's causing the burning so we can choose the right treatment. Can you tell me more about your symptoms, including when they began?
reply: The burning is worst at the end of urinating, like my last UTI. I've been going all the time — every half hour — but only a little comes out each time. It's been happening since yesterday morning, so about a day and a half. The urine is a bit cloudy and smells, but I haven't seen any blood.

awards.label: How long the symptoms have been present
Colour of the urine or any visible blood

utterance: Have you had any fever, chills, pain in your back or sides, nausea or vomiting? Do you have any pain low in your tummy?
reply: No, I haven't had any fever, chills, nausea or vomiting. I don't have pain in my back or sides, just a bit of a low ache above my bladder. I'm eating normally and feeling fine apart from the burning when I urinate.

awards.label: Red flag excluded: Fever, sweats, chills or shaking
Red flag excluded: Pain in the back or sides (loins)
Red flag excluded: Nausea, vomiting or feeling generally unwell
Red flag excluded: Abdominal pain beyond a low ache

utterance: Any vaginal discharge, itching, sores, unusual bleeding, or pain during sex? When was your last period, and is there any chance you could be pregnant?
reply: No, I haven't had any vaginal discharge, itching, sores or unusual bleeding. I've never had pain during sex or bleeding after sex, and nothing between my periods. My last period was about two weeks ago and it was normal. I don't think I'm pregnant.

awards.label: Bleeding after sex or between periods
Red flag excluded: Whether she could be pregnant

utterance: Have you missed any contraceptive pills recently? Have you had a new sexual partner or sex without condoms, and when were you last tested for sexually transmitted infections?
reply: No, I haven't missed any contraceptive pills recently. I have a boyfriend, we've been together about a year, and we don't use condoms because I'm on the pill. We'd been together the night before it started.

awards.label: Recent sexual intercourse as a possible trigger

utterance: Have you or your boyfriend had other partners in that time, and have you had a sexual infection test before? How many urine infections have you had before, and what treatment worked?
reply: No, my boyfriend and I haven't had other partners in that time. I haven't had a sexual infection test before. I had one UTI about two years ago, that's it. The treatment worked, but I don't remember exactly what it was.

utterance: Have you ever had kidney problems, kidney stones, diabetes, or surgery or procedures on your urinary system? Are you taking anything besides the pill, including treatment for these symptoms, and do you have any medicine allergies?
reply: No, I haven't had any kidney problems, kidney stones, diabetes or surgery on my urinary system. I'm only taking the pill and I'm not allergic to anything that I know of.

utterance: Your symptoms sound like a bladder infection. With your permission I'll check your temperature, pulse and blood pressure, and gently feel your tummy and check over your kidneys. I'd also like a urine sample to check for infection.
reply: Okay, that's fine. I'll do the urine test. I just want to get this sorted and back to work.

finding: Soft. Mild suprapubic tenderness; non-tender elsewhere. No masses or organomegaly.
No renal angle tenderness on either side.

result: Leucocytes ++, nitrites positive, blood trace, protein trace. hCG not tested.

utterance: The urine test supports a bladder infection, and there's no sign of a kidney infection. Because pregnancy would change treatment decisions, are you happy for us to do a pregnancy test too? Also, we routinely offer chlamydia and gonorrhoea screening to sexually active people under 30, even without symptoms; would you like that screening?
reply: I'm happy for the pregnancy test. I don't know about the chlamydia and gonorrhoea screening — I guess it's better to be safe.

utterance: These infections can be present without symptoms, so screening doesn't mean I think either of you has been unfaithful. It's optional and confidential. It can be done with a self-collected vaginal swab, which is the most accurate sample for women. Would you like to go ahead with that?
reply: I guess I'll go ahead with the screening. I'm not sure how it works, but I'll do it.

utterance: Your pregnancy test is negative. Have you used any antibiotics in the last three months, or ever been told you have G6PD deficiency, an inherited condition that can cause red blood cells to break down with certain medicines?
reply: No, I haven't used any antibiotics this year. I don't think I've ever been told I have G6PD deficiency.

awards.label: Antibiotics in the last few months
First-line antibiotic: nitrofurantoin 100 mg 6-hourly for 5 days, fosfomycin 3 g once, or trimethoprim 300 mg daily for 3 days

utterance:
I'm prescribing nitrofurantoin: one 100 mg capsule four times a day with food for five days. Finish the course. It can cause nausea and turn urine darker yellow or brown, which is harmless. If you develop a rash, stop it and seek advice; trouble breathing or swelling of your lips or tongue needs emergency help. It doesn't reduce the pill's effectiveness, but vomiting or significant diarrhoea can—follow your pill's missed-dose instructions if that happens.

Drink enough water to avoid dehydration, without forcing large amounts, and don't hold your urine. You can take paracetamol for discomfort, 500 mg to 1 gram up to four times a day, at least four hours apart, maximum 4 grams daily. Avoid urinary alkalinising sachets such as Ural while taking this antibiotic because they can make it less effective. Avoid sex until you're comfortable; emptying your bladder after sex is reasonable, though not guaranteed to prevent infections.

For the screening swab, the kit comes with instructions: gently insert the swab into the vagina, rotate it as directed and return it to the tube. I'll arrange contact about the result in about two days; if you haven't heard within a few days, please contact us.

You should start feeling better within 24–48 hours. If you're not improving within 48 hours, or symptoms return after treatment, come back so we can send urine to the laboratory and review treatment. Seek urgent care the same day if you get fever, shaking chills, back or side pain, vomiting, worsening tummy pain, or feel very unwell. If you're faint, confused or severely unwell, call 000. Does that plan work for you, or do you have any questions?
reply: Yeah, that plan works for me. I'll take the antibiotic and do the screening. I'll keep drinking water and try to finish the course. I'll call if I'm not better in a couple of days.

awards.label: Reasonable differential: Urethritis from a sexually transmitted infection
